    Ube Donuts

    Posted On September 14, 2026 By Mirlene Last updated August 26, 2026 Leave a Comment

    Share this recipe:

    Jump to Recipe

    Instaread

    These homemade Filipino Ube Donuts are so ridiculously soft, fluffy, and flavored with ube before being fried until beautifully golden.

    We’re making these with yeast rather than baking powder, so the texture is light and pillowy instead of cake-like.

    For this Filipino Ube Donut recipe, you can use ube extract or ube powder depending on what you have available, then finish the donuts with your favorite frosting or creamy filling.

    And if you’ve been looking for another excuse to keep ube in the pantry…Here you go. 💜

    What Is Ube?

    Ube is a purple yam commonly used in Filipino desserts. It has a subtly sweet, slightly nutty flavor and is known for giving desserts that gorgeous purple color.

    For these donuts, you can use ube extract or ube powder.

    The two don’t work exactly the same way, though.

    Ube Extract vs. Ube Powder

    Ube extract provides concentrated flavor and usually stronger purple coloring, so you only need ½ teaspoon for this recipe.

    Ube powder is less concentrated. Start with the 3 teaspoons in the recipe and adjust if needed based on the product you’re using and the color/flavor you want.

    My Special Tips For Perfect Filipino Donuts

    Watch the water temperature (important). Aim for approximately 115°F. You want warm water—not scorching hot water.

    Add ube extract to the liquid. If you’re using ube powder, mix it with the dry ingredients so it distributes more evenly.

    Don’t add extra flour too quickly. Give the dough time to come together during kneading before deciding it needs additional flour.

    Don’t rush either rise. Give the dough 1 hour to 1 and 30 minutes (depending on the temperature of your home or proofing section) to properly rise until doubled in size. This is key to a perfectly soft donut. Then, let the shaped donuts rise another 30 minutes or until doubled.

    Keep your oil around 330- but no more than 350°F. Too hot and the outside can brown before the center cooks. Too cool and the donuts can absorb excess oil.

    Few Questions You May Have When Making These Donuts

    What does ube taste like?

    Ube has a mild sweetness with slightly nutty and vanilla-like notes. Its flavor is subtle, which is why it’s often paired with vanilla, coconut and other creamy flavors.

    Can I use ube powder instead of ube extract?

    Yes. This recipe allows for either. Use approximately ½ teaspoon ube extract or 3 teaspoons ube powder, adjusting the powder if necessary, depending on the product.

    Why aren’t my ube donuts bright purple?

    The final color depends heavily on the ube product you’re using. Ube extract generally produces a much brighter purple than ube powder, and natural ube colors can change somewhat during cooking.

    How To Make Ube Donuts

    Soft & Fluffy Ube Donuts Recipe

    Savory Thoughts
    Soft and fluffy Filipino yeast-raised Ube Donuts made with ube extract or ube powder, fried until golden and finished with your favorite creamy vanilla filling
    No ratings yet
    Print Recipe Pin Recipe
    Prep Time 15 minutes mins
    Cook Time 15 minutes mins
    Rising Time 1 hour hr 45 minutes mins
    Total Time 2 hours hrs 15 minutes mins
    Course Dessert
    Cuisine Filipino
    Servings 18 donuts
    Calories 164 kcal

    Equipment

    • Stand Mixer
    • Mixing Bowls

    Ingredients
      

    • 1 cup + 2 Tbsp. warm water about 115°F
    • 2 Tbsp. powdered whole milk
    • 1½ Tbsp. granulated sugar
    • 1 tsp. kosher salt
    • 3 cups bread flour
    • 1½ tsp. instant yeast
    • ½ tsp. ube extract OR 3 tsp. ube powder or as needed
    • 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter softened
    • 1 Tbsp. vegetable oil
    • Neutral oil for frying
    • Desired frosting or filling

    Instructions
     

    • Make The Ube Dough
      In a large measuring cup or bowl, combine the warm water, powdered whole milk, sugar, and kosher salt. If using ube extract, add it to the liquid mixture.
      Add the bread flour and instant yeast to the bowl of a stand mixer. If using ube powder, add it to the flour mixture. Mix well to combine. 
      Attach the dough hook, starting with the lowest speed level, pour the liquid mixture into the dry ingredients and add the vegetable oil.
      Continue kneading on low speed. 
      Once the dough begins coming together, gradually add the softened butter.
      Continue kneading until the dough is smooth and elastic. This process should take about 15 minutes on low speed (if using the KitchenAid stand mixer, no more than speed 2)
      Transfer to a lightly greased bowl and cover. Allow the dough to rise for 1 hour or more in a warm place until double in size.
    • Shape, Rise & Fry
      Gently deflate the dough with a clean hand and transfer it to a lightly floured work surface.
      Roll out the dough and cut into the desired donut shape. Be sure to keep the shapes at even size. 
      Transfer the donuts to parchment paper, cover loosely, and allow them to rise for 30 minutes or until doubled in size.
      Heat neutral oil to 330°F – but no more than 350°F. If the oil is too hot, it will burn the donuts. 
    • Working in batches, fry the donuts for approximately 2–4 minutes or until golden, turning as necessary.
      Transfer to a wire rack or paper-towel-lined tray.
      Allow to cool enough to handle. Dust with granulated sugar if desired. 
      Create a small opening in each donut and pipe in your desired frosting or filling.

    Notes

    How The Ingredients Work In This Recipe

    Bread flour: Gives the yeast dough enough structure while keeping the finished donuts soft and chewy.
    Instant yeast: Creates the airy, fluffy interior.
    Ube extract or powder: Gives our donuts their signature ube flavor and color.
    Powdered whole milk: Adds richness without changing the amount of liquid in the dough.
    Unsalted butter: Makes the dough softer and richer.
    Vegetable oil: A small amount further enriches the dough.

     

    How To Store Your Ube Donuts

    These donuts are best enjoyed the day they’re fried.
    Unfilled donuts can be kept in an airtight container at room temperature for about 1–2 days.
    Once filled, storage depends on the filling. Donuts filled with cream cheese, whipped cream, custard or another perishable filling should be refrigerated.
